claims.claim: Sanctions-evasion risk can shift toward intermediary routing through Central Asia and Caspian trade corridors.
claims.uncertainty: Trade data is aggregate and lagged; corridor-level attribution requires additional analysis.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Compliance teams over-tag corridors and miss other higher-risk routing channels.

claims.claim: OFAC and FATF materials provide official context for evasion-risk analysis.
claims.uncertainty: Designation lists do not by themselves quantify routing volumes.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Briefings imply more granular official guidance than actually exists.

claims.claim: An exact share of evasion transactions routed through Caspian corridors is known.
claims.uncertainty: No public dataset aggregates beneficial ownership at corridor level.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Numeric claims in deliverables cite a precision no source supports.

evidence.name: OFAC Sanctions Programs and Country Information
supports: Official sanctions-program context and designation updates
limits: Identifies targets, not full trade-routing volumes

evidence.name: FATF Publications
supports: Official AML/CFT typologies and regional risk material
limits: Broad typology material may not prove a specific corridor shift

evidence.name: UN Comtrade database
supports: Trade-flow checks for anomalies by product, partner, and route proxy
limits: Lagged and aggregate; does not prove intent or beneficial ownership

unsupported_claims: Exact proportion of sanctions-evasion transactions routed through Central Asia or Caspian corridors
